name: User Typed Paths
purpose: Records paths a user manually typed or pasted into the File Explorer address/path bar, including local paths and remote UNC paths to network shares. Proves deliberate navigation to a specific location rather than passive browsing.
key_fields: Value names - url1, url2, url3, ... sequential
Value data - the literal path or UNC string the user typed (e.g. C:\Users\jdoe\Desktop\staging, \\fileserver\hr$)
Key LastWrite time - when the most recent typed path was committed
normal_baseline: A handful of familiar local folders and known network shares the user regularly navigates to by typing rather than clicking through folder hierarchies.
anomalies: UNC paths to unfamiliar internal hosts or admin shares (\\host\C$, \\host\ADMIN$) typed by a user with no administrative reason to browse them
Paths into other users' profile directories
Typed paths to removable/external drive letters or mount points not otherwise associated with that user
Typed paths referencing staging or exfiltration-style folder names shortly before large file transfers or archive creation evidenced elsewhere
Key entries present with a LastWrite time inconsistent with the newest url# value, suggesting manual edits to the underlying hive
anti_forensic_notes: An entry is only written to the registry once the File Explorer window is closed, so a typed path used and abandoned mid-session in a still-open window will not appear in an acquired hive. TypedPaths is not cleared by mainstream privacy/cleanup tools (CCleaner, BleachBit, Windows Disk Cleanup), so its presence is comparatively reliable, but the key's LastWrite time reflects when Explorer was closed, not the moment the path was typed.
